author: NewsBreak
title: FBI Returns Rare Hernán Cortés Manuscript to Mexico in New York Ceremony - NewsBreak
text: NEW YORK – The FBI has returned a stolen 16th century manuscript signed by Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés to the government of Mexico during an August 13, 2025 ceremony. "This is an original manuscript page that was actually signed by Hernán Cortés on February 20, 1527," said Special Agent Jessica Dittmer of the FBI’s Art Crime Team. She explained that the document “outlines the payment of pesos of common gold for expenses in preparation for discovery of the spice lands,” offering insight into the planning for uncharted expeditions. Authorities believe the page—part of Mexico’s national archives—was stolen between 1985 and 1993. In 2024, Mexico asked the FBI Art Crime Team to locate the missing page. NYPD Detective Rigel Zeledon said the recovery “could not have been possible without the collaboration of the Southern District of New York” and the FBI’s attaché in Mexico. Investigators relied on meticulous archival notes, including page numbers and tear marks, to authenticate the artifact. The search eventually led them to the continental United States, where FBI Atlanta and federal prosecutors helped secure legal possession. Dittmer said stakeholders in possession of the page signed away claims, allowing the FBI to verify and return it. No charges will be filed, as the document changed hands many times. Dittmer hopes the recovery deters cultural thefts and emphasizes the importance of repatriation. This is the FBI’s second such success—following a 2023 return of another Cortés document. The FBI Art Crime Team continues to search for the remaining missing pages. Tips can be submitted at tips.fbi.gov or by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI.
